about.eyebrow: Mechanical Engineering — Stevens Institute of Technology
about.bodyP1: I'm a mechanical engineering student at Stevens Institute of Technology. I constantly seek out the most difficult challenges in any environment, and I always try to uplift those around me to leave things better than I found them. I constantly seek novel experiences and new ways to explain the world. One of the biggest motivators in my life is to ensure that no one feels forgotten and to do what I can, when I can, to help others.
about.school: Stevens Institute of Technology, Hoboken NJ
coursework: Frontiers of Tech: A.I. & Machine Learning

statements.head: Why aerospace
statements.text: When I was young, I heard stories and read books that described small teams pushing the edge of human capability and creating engineering marvels. This idea of how teams can work together and what they can achieve has informed many of my decisions since then. This desire to work in groups to solve difficult problems is why I have dedicated a great deal of time to the SAE Baja team. The way teams are set up to work closely with the machine floor and do things fast makes me really excited for not only our nation but also the engineering field as a whole.

statements.head: Always learning
statements.text: I am a junior mechanical engineering student at Stevens Institute of Technology. I constantly push myself to learn more and prepare for the next challenge. I believe this mentality is reflected in how, by the end of my sophomore year, I was selected to be the president of the most technically challenging club on campus, taught a class in which I learned material outside the school curriculum, acquired a $100,000 machine for the school without a formal process existing, and started summer research. I have learned a great deal from these experiences, but I know there is so much more to go. No matter the environment, I always strive to do my best work and collaborate with others.

statements.head: Leading SAE Baja
statements.text: I have been part of SAE Baja for the past three years, designing, manufacturing, and assembling three vehicles, each outperforming the last. Proving my technical ability and leadership early on, I quickly rose through the ranks. By the end of my second year, I had designed and fabricated the braking system, served on the executive board as recording secretary, and was elected president for the upcoming year. I currently lead 40-plus members, coordinate subteams, set project timelines, and oversee overall vehicle design. Through this experience, I have developed strong problem-solving skills, learned to drive projects independently, and mentored team members to achieve technical goals. With my aptitude for project-based engineering, I now teach a class on the technical know-how of taking an idea through the engineering process to the final manufactured part they create themselves on CNC equipment.

statements.head: Earning trust
statements.text: In both my work and daily life, I consistently earn the trust of those around me. I have taken this approach from a young age, through high school and now college. I have done so by staying methodical, dependable, and never demanding of others. In high school, I demonstrated my trustworthiness in academic and extracurricular settings, which led to my roles as captain of the squash team, manager of the cross-country team, film club president, student government member, committee member overseeing future school curriculum, and recipient of half a dozen awards. In college, I have continued this approach as a core part of who I am; today, I work in a campus machine shop, instruct a class, and serve as president of the SAE Baja team. These accomplishments have only been possible because I consistently show up positively for the people in my life. I met deadlines, exceeded expectations, empathized with others, and earned their trust along the way.

statements.head: Learning outside the classroom
statements.text: From the beginning of college, I knew there would be many things I wouldn't learn in class, so I have spent most of my free time learning outside the normal curriculum. Within the first couple of weeks of freshman year, I started taking part in the SAE BAJA team. I was exposed to an entirely new world where we not only had to design all of the cars but also manufacture them ourselves. In time, I learned how to operate CNC mills, Lathes, plasma cutters, laser cutters, and TIG welders. I enjoyed learning how to use these tools and their advantages and disadvantages, but I see them for what they are: tools. They are the end to a means. I've grown most in my design ability. I learned early on what causes clearance problems between parts and what doesn't integrate, the importance of using standards whenever possible, and to define the goals and constraints of the design before I start my first sketch. I also learned a great deal about applying DFM, FEA, and CFD when working on the car. I learned how to take a design through concepting, design, machining, testing, integration, and finalization. I have learned how to perform in high-stress situations while working in a group.

projects.title: SAE BAJA: Fabrication & Training
paragraphs: This year, I am fabricating suspension parts, carbon fiber body panels, and the braking system.
I can now TIG weld with such strength that the tube bends before the weld breaks. I now teach all incoming new students how to weld on the frame of the car and how to do so safely.
For any given part, I use DFM, CFD, and FEA in my design process.

projects.title: Autonomous Boat Design
paragraphs: Led a student engineering team through brainstorming, planning, and rapid prototyping of an autonomous boat, designing the ship hull and internal wiring architecture.
Utilized CFD and FEA to test and iterate 3D-printed hull and electronics housing designs, culminating in a comprehensive technical report and presentation.
I tested multiple hull designs, ultimately choosing a catamaran for its excellent stability at slow speeds.

projects.title: Automatic Door Opener
paragraphs: Designed a mechanism to open a dorm room door remotely from a phone app.
3D printed components, coded an Arduino/servo motor system, installed the design on the door, and debugged hardware/software issues.
Presented the project to other students, explaining the process and inspiration behind it.

projects.title: Automatic Plant Waterer
paragraphs: Led a team of three in fabricating an automatic plant watering system.
Used SolidWorks to concept and design the electronic enclosure, and Arduino to program the watering logic.
3D printed the final product and calibrated the system to feed water at optimal times.

projects.title: Electroplating
paragraphs: Conducted independent online research to understand the process and science behind electroplating.
Nickel-plated and copper-plated various items, such as coins and rings, after developing a working process.
